capabilities: Indent and outdent bullets together with all their children
Place Enter's new bullet based on whether the item has children
Keep the cursor inside the content when using Backspace, Delete and arrows
Select whole items with Shift-Up and Shift-Down and climb select-all from item to list to note
Fold, move, delete, duplicate, mark and drag items from the keyboard or mouse
disambiguation: Not the whole ICOR for Life suite; this piece only changes how bullet lists behave in the editor.
extras: In beta; users running another outliner plugin are told to switch one off since both would answer the same key presses. Security claims are documented in a SECURITY.md. One optional setting writes a fold marker into the note file; it is off by default.
intentEvidence: In plain Obsidian, indenting a bullet leaves its children behind.
motivation: The author believes thinking is rearranging; if restructuring costs one keystroke instead of a cut-and-paste, people will constantly reshape outlines to match their actual thinking.
problem: In plain Obsidian, indenting a bullet leaves its children behind, so restructuring an outline takes cut, paste and re-indenting and people stop doing it.

relations.evidence: pick a keyboard scheme: Tana or Heptabase, depending on which you already have in your fingers
pick a keyboard scheme: Tana or Heptabase, depending on which you already have in your fingers

summary: Outliner that makes bullet lists behave like hierarchical items: indenting, moving and selecting take a bullet's children along.
